name: Swansea
label: Head office
partner_bio: Hello New Home started here. The office on Central Business Park is where every area's contracts, compliance and rent collection are run from.
covers: Swansea, Mumbles, Gower, Neath, Port Talbot and Llanelli
demand: Swansea University and the Bay Campus, Morriston and Singleton hospitals, the Arena and the Marina for short stays, and year-round Gower and Mumbles tourism.
licensing: Additional HMO licensing covers Castle, Uplands, St Thomas and Waterfront wards from 14 February 2026; mandatory licensing applies to larger HMOs citywide. Every landlord must be registered with Rent Smart Wales.
shortlet: Swansea has short-stay demand around the Arena and the Marina through the year, Gower and Mumbles from Easter to September, and the university and hospitals for stays of a few nights to a few weeks. The Wales visitor accommodation register opened 1 October 2026; existing providers must register by 31 March 2027. The 182-night business-rates test applies.
rent_note: ONS average private rent for Swansea, May 2026, with the annual change. Your rent review uses current lets street by street.

name: Durham
label: Local Partner
partner_bio: [Two lines: how long they've lived in County Durham, what they do locally, why landlords should trust them.]
covers: Durham City, Chester-le-Street, Consett, Stanley, Bishop Auckland, Newton Aycliffe and County Durham
demand: Durham University students and staff, University Hospital of North Durham, Newton Aycliffe's industrial park and commuters to Newcastle and Teesside, plus cathedral-city tourism for short stays.
licensing: County Durham runs a selective licensing scheme: every privately rented home inside the designated areas needs a licence from Durham County Council, and a successor scheme is being consulted on for 2027. We check your address and handle the application. HMO rules follow the England mandatory threshold of five or more people from two or more households.
shortlet: The England business-rates test for self-catering is 140 nights available and 70 nights let; Durham County Council charges a 100% council-tax premium on second homes that miss it. Cathedral-city and university demand supports short stays in and around Durham City through the year, with graduation and conference weeks the peaks.
rent_note: ONS average private rent for County Durham, August 2026, with the annual change. At these rents our 12% fee is well under the cap, so you simply pay 12% with no VAT and nothing else.

name: Andover
label: Local Partner
partner_bio: [Two lines: how long they've lived in Test Valley, what they do locally, why landlords should trust them.]
covers: Andover, Ludgershall, Tidworth, Whitchurch, Stockbridge and the Test Valley
demand: The Army at Tidworth and Larkhill, Ocado and Andover's logistics and business parks, commuters on the Waterloo line, and relocations from Basingstoke, Winchester and Salisbury.
licensing: Test Valley has no selective or additional licensing scheme at present, so only larger HMOs (five or more people from two or more households) need a licence. We check for any change before marketing.
shortlet: The England business-rates test for self-catering is 140 nights available and 70 nights let; Test Valley charges a 100% council-tax premium on second homes. Demand is contractor and military-family led rather than tourist led, which suits stays of a month or more and keeps the calendar steady through the winter.
rent_note: ONS average private rent for Test Valley, June 2026, with the annual change; typical one-beds around £880 and two-beds around £1,135. The £150 cap saves most Andover landlords money from the first month.

name: London
label: Local Partner
partner_bio: Ina is the founder of Divitiae Acquisitions, which sources property and matches investors with deals across London and the UK, and she runs our London lettings and short-let management. Her focus is simple: an honest rent figure and a property that is looked after.
covers: Every London borough, from the City and the West End to Bromley, Croydon, Harrow, Havering, Hillingdon and Kingston
places: Central London and the City fringe
demand: The largest rental market in the country: professionals, students at every university, hospital and relocation lets, and a short-stay market that runs all year on hospital contractors, relocating professionals, events and visitors, with month-plus stays filling the quieter weeks.
licensing: Licensing is borough by borough: many London boroughs run additional or selective licensing on top of mandatory HMO licensing, and several charge a 100% council-tax premium on second homes. We check the borough for every address before marketing.
shortlet: London short stays earn in every season: hospital contractors, relocating professionals, students between tenancies, events and visitors. Our London SA offer prices by the season, keeps a pipeline of month-plus contractor and relocation lets for the quieter weeks, and uses Flex Switch to move to a tenancy if that wins. The England business-rates test (140 nights available, 70 let) applies.
rent_note: ONS average private rent for London, August 2026, with the annual change; inner boroughs average higher, outer boroughs lower. At £2,332 a 12% fee would be £280 a month; ours is £150. The cap matters more in London than anywhere else we work.

name: Somerset
label: Local Partner
partner_bio: Martin Howard founded Hello New Home, and in Somerset he is the one at your door. He lives here and does the photographs, viewings, move-ins, move-outs and quarterly inspections himself, writes the report and takes your calls. He also runs Somerset Lettings, founded Property Predator, which analyses rents, yields and deals, and mentors property investors. Whatever happens at your house, the person answering for it started the company.
covers: Taunton, Bridgwater, Yeovil, Wells, Glastonbury, Frome, Weston-super-Mare, Clevedon, Bath and the rest of Somerset
demand: Hinkley Point C's contractor workforce around Bridgwater, Musgrove Park Hospital and the county offices in Taunton, Leonardo Helicopters in Yeovil, the University of Bath and Bath Spa University, M5 commuters to Bristol, and tourism across Exmoor, Cheddar, the coast and Glastonbury.
licensing: Somerset Council runs mandatory HMO licensing (five or more people from two or more households) and no additional or selective scheme was in force when we checked. Bath and North East Somerset is mandatory licensing only, its additional scheme having ended on 31 December 2023. We check the council for every address before marketing.
shortlet: The England business-rates test for self-catering is 140 nights available and 70 nights let. Somerset's short-stay demand mixes Hinkley Point contractors and hospital staff on month-plus stays with Exmoor, Cheddar, coast and Glastonbury visitors in the season, so a well-run calendar earns all year.
rent_note: ONS average private rent for Somerset, August 2026, with the annual change; Bath and North East Somerset averages £1,885 and North Somerset about £1,209. At £1,016 our 12% fee is about £122 a month with no VAT; in Bath, where rents average £1,885, the £150 cap saves you money from the first month.
